variants.title: Extract in order
variants.context: Migrate gradually: name the constraint, prove a boundary in-process, extract a narrow path behind a router while retaining the old path, then transfer deployment, on-call, data ownership, and recovery responsibility.
variants.prompt: A team wants to extract shipping quotes. Put the migration steps in order.

items.text: Put a router in front of the capability, keep the old path, and move traffic only when observable.
Prove the boundary in-process with one vocabulary, one write owner, and an interface.
Name the constraint: the blocked release, overloaded capability, or ownership conflict.
Transfer deployment, on-call, data ownership, objectives, and recovery with the capability.

variants.hint: A boundary must be proven inside the monolith before it crosses the network.
variants.explanation: Measure → modularize → strangle → operate. A migration is not a rewrite.

variants.title: Extract in order
variants.context: Migrate gradually: name the constraint, prove a boundary in-process, extract a narrow path behind a router while retaining the old path, then transfer deployment, on-call, data ownership, and recovery responsibility.
variants.prompt: An extraction is being planned for notifications. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Move alerts, dashboards, and the recovery runbook to the owning team.
Route one narrow path through the new service behind a rollback switch.
Capture the measurable constraint it must remove.
Enforce a module API and prohibit cross-module table access.

variants.hint: The old path stays runnable until comparison and rollback are proven.
variants.explanation: Ownership transfer completes the extraction, not the first deploy.

variants.title: Extract in order
variants.context: Migrate gradually: name the constraint, prove a boundary in-process, extract a narrow path behind a router while retaining the old path, then transfer deployment, on-call, data ownership, and recovery responsibility.
variants.prompt: A previous attempt split the database first and only added network hops. Put the corrected order.

items.text: Give the module one write owner in-process.
Transfer operational ownership.
Extract a narrow path with the router and observability in place.
Start from the constraint, not the table.

variants.hint: A shared-database split is not a business boundary.
variants.explanation: Extract cohesive business capabilities, not technical layers.

variants.title: Decide the boundary
variants.context: Extract when a team, load profile, release cadence, or reliability requirement needs independent control. Keep the monolith when business rules are still being discovered, a single transaction protects the core invariant, or the team cannot yet operate a separate service.
variants.prompt: The domain’s business rules are still changing weekly. Extract now?
options: Yes; a service boundary forces the rules to be clear.
Yes, but split into just two services for now.
No; a boundary now would freeze guesses into contracts.
optionFeedback: A network contract does not clarify rules; it locks in this week's guess.
Two boundaries are still two guesses frozen while the domain moves.
Unstable language is a signal to keep the monolith.
variants.explanation: Start with a modular monolith when the domain is still changing.

variants.title: Decide the boundary
variants.context: Extract when a team, load profile, release cadence, or reliability requirement needs independent control. Keep the monolith when business rules are still being discovered, a single transaction protects the core invariant, or the team cannot yet operate a separate service.
variants.prompt: One capability uses ten times the CPU of the rest and blocks scaling. Extract?
options: Only after the whole app is decomposed.
Yes, if the team can operate it separately.
No; scale the whole application instead.
optionFeedback: Independent scaling is a concrete constraint a boundary removes.
Scaling everything to match one hot capability wastes the rest of the fleet.
variants.hint: Which concrete constraint would the boundary remove?
variants.explanation: Extract only when a specific capability needs independent control.

variants.title: Decide the boundary
variants.context: Extract when a team, load profile, release cadence, or reliability requirement needs independent control. Keep the monolith when business rules are still being discovered, a single transaction protects the core invariant, or the team cannot yet operate a separate service.
variants.prompt: Leadership measures maturity by service count. What is the better metric?
options: Independently managed contracts and recovery paths.
The number of services owned per team.
optionFeedback: Ten services owned by ten teams can be simpler than ten owned by two.
Services per team is still a count, and it says nothing about coupling.
Fewer is not automatically better either.
variants.hint: What does each additional service cost?
variants.explanation: Count what must be independently managed.

variants.title: Estimate the extraction
variants.context: Estimate the extraction: downstream requests per second, capacity with headroom, and retry amplification, plus explicit latency, availability, and consistency budgets.
variants.prompt: Checkout peaks at 2,000 requests per second and 30% need a shipping quote. How many downstream shipping requests per second does a synchronous call add?
variants.hint: Multiply peak by the fraction that needs the call.
variants.explanation: 2,000 × 0.3 = 600 requests per second to the new service.

mistakes.feedback: Only 30% of requests need the quote.

variants.title: Estimate the extraction
variants.context: Estimate the extraction: downstream requests per second, capacity with headroom, and retry amplification, plus explicit latency, availability, and consistency budgets.
variants.prompt: The new service must sustain 600 requests per second with 40% headroom. What capacity should be planned before retries?
variants.explanation: 600 ÷ 0.6 = 1,000 requests per second of sustainable capacity.

mistakes.feedback: Headroom means 600 is only 60% of capacity, not 140% of demand.

variants.title: Estimate the extraction
variants.context: Estimate the extraction: downstream requests per second, capacity with headroom, and retry amplification, plus explicit latency, availability, and consistency budgets.
variants.prompt: A retry policy doubles calls during a timeout. What downstream rate can 600 requests per second become?
variants.explanation: 600 × 2 = 1,200, which consumes the 1,000 capacity plan immediately. Bound retries.

mistakes.feedback: The retry doubles 600, not the whole checkout rate.

variants.title: Promote safely
variants.context: Promote safely: mirror or shadow eligible reads, canary a small cohort, expand with a stop rule and observation window, roll back before repair.
variants.prompt: The new fulfillment path is ready. Put the promotion in order.

items.text: Expand only after a healthy observation window, keeping the previous path compatible.
Canary a small identifiable cohort with alerts on errors, latency, correctness, and fallback volume.
Mirror or shadow eligible reads to the candidate and compare results without changing responses.
If a guardrail breaches, route back first and diagnose from request IDs and retained comparisons.

variants.hint: Reads before irreversible writes when possible.
variants.explanation: Shadow → canary → expand with a stop rule → roll back before repair.

variants.title: Promote safely
variants.context: Promote safely: mirror or shadow eligible reads, canary a small cohort, expand with a stop rule and observation window, roll back before repair.
variants.prompt: A write path is being moved. Put the steps in order.

items.text: On breach, roll back before repairing.
Route a small cohort’s writes with idempotency keys and correlated logs.
Increase traffic per the observation window.
Shadow the equivalent reads and compare.

variants.explanation: Keep old and new paths runnable long enough to compare, roll back, and reconcile.

variants.title: Promote safely
variants.context: Promote safely: mirror or shadow eligible reads, canary a small cohort, expand with a stop rule and observation window, roll back before repair.
variants.prompt: A canary shows a correctness regression. Put the response in order.

items.text: The correctness alert fires on the cohort.
Route back to the previous path first, then diagnose.
Shadowing had matched; the canary was the first real exposure.
Stop promotion at the stop rule.

variants.hint: The stop rule exists so nobody has to improvise.
variants.explanation: Roll back before repair; diagnose from retained comparison data.

variants.title: Keep the boundary honest
variants.context: A service owns its writes and publishes facts; other services use its API or events, never its tables. A replicated copy is not a second write owner. Degrade optional paths; fail closed on the business invariant.
variants.prompt: The shipping service reads the orders table directly for speed. What is wrong?
options: Other services must go through the order API or events.
Nothing is wrong, because a read changes nothing.
It should write to the orders table as well.
optionFeedback: Table access couples the schema and defeats the boundary.
A read still binds shipping to the order schema and blocks schema changes.
Adding writes gives one fact two owners, which is worse still.
variants.explanation: A service owns its writes and publishes facts.

variants.title: Keep the boundary honest
variants.context: A service owns its writes and publishes facts; other services use its API or events, never its tables. A replicated copy is not a second write owner. Degrade optional paths; fail closed on the business invariant.
variants.prompt: The shipping screen keeps an asynchronous copy of the order address. Is it a second write owner?
options: Yes, if the copy updates often enough.
No; it is a read model with a known source.
Yes, any stored copy is a write owner.
optionFeedback: Read models duplicate deliberately; the order service still owns the fact.
Storing a copy is not owning the fact; the order service still owns it.
variants.explanation: Let read models duplicate data deliberately, with a known source.

variants.title: Keep the boundary honest
variants.context: A service owns its writes and publishes facts; other services use its API or events, never its tables. A replicated copy is not a second write owner. Degrade optional paths; fail closed on the business invariant.
variants.prompt: Payment authorization is unavailable during checkout. What should the order do?
options: Fail closed; never claim the order is paid.
Mark it paid and reconcile the difference later.
Skip the payment step for this order.
optionFeedback: Degrade optional paths; fail closed on the business invariant.
Payment is the invariant here, so skipping it ships unpaid orders.
variants.hint: Which promise must never be false?
variants.explanation: Failure isolation is a product decision.
